core_obligations: Double-induction setup (proof lines 482-494): define comparability, induct on alpha over ordinals each comparable with every ordinal, and inside that on beta, reducing to showing alpha comparable with beta under outer hypotheses.
Membership is impossible by assumption (lines 494-496): it suffices to assume not(alpha in beta) and not(beta in alpha) and prove alpha = beta.
Inclusion alpha c beta (lines 497-503): fix gamma in alpha; the induction hypothesis makes gamma comparable with beta, the two wrong alternatives land beta in alpha, so gamma in beta; generalise.
Symmetric inclusion (lines 504-506): the second induction hypothesis gives beta c alpha identically; extensionality yields alpha = beta.
proof_roadmap: Set up the nested induction on alpha, then beta, via the ordinal induction schema.
Assume neither membership direction and aim for equality.
Push each element of alpha into beta using the induction hypothesis and transitivity.
Repeat symmetrically for beta into alpha.
difficulty_reason: A textbook double-induction argument (statement 477-480, proof 482-506) with every case closure explicit; the reader must track two nested induction hypotheses but no construction beyond them. H2: standard ordinal trichotomy with all bookkeeping present.
